1. Dissatisfied by the grant of meager compensation in M.A.C.P. No. 178 of 2009 decided on 05.01.2012 by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Beed, original claimants have come up in appeal.

2. In short, On 22.05.2009, between 1:00 p.m. and 1:30 FA-1910-2012 p.m., the deceased Smita along with her sister Priyanka, was proceeding towards Jalna from their college via the Aurangabad- Jalna Highway on a Scooty bearing No. MH-23-M-1721.
Smita was then pillion rider while Priyanka was riding the Scooty.
When they reached near Yash Dhaba Hotel and Patani Farm, an S.T. bus bearing No. MH-12-AV-9076 came from backside in a rash and negligent manner and gave dash to Scooty.
As a result, both Smita and Priyanka fell down.

They were taken to Deepak Hospital, Jalna,

3. Learned counsel for original claimants would point out that, on account of demise of Smita Madhusudan Khedkar, a daughter of original claimants - appellants, in a road traffic accident dated 22.05.2009, above claim was instituted by invoking section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
4. It is further submitted that, learned Tribunal has merely considered meager income of deceased as Rs.3,000/- per month.
That, in similar cases, this court had considered income to the tune of Rs.10,000/- to 11,000/- and the copies of said rulings are placed on record.

In support of above contentions he seeks reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Navjot Singh v.
FA-1910-2012 Harpreet Singh & Ors., 2020(2) SimLC 685 : 2020 (1) TAC 736 and the decision of the High Court of Bombay, Nagpur Bench in the case of Khalid Ansari and Ors. v. Aebhalbhai Babubhai Vegad and Ors. in First Appeal No.1612 of 2019.

6. Learned counsel for respondent Shri Bagul would justify the award passed by learned Tribunal and prays to dismiss the appeal for want of merits.
7.
Heard.
Perused the impugned Judgment.

It is emerging that, on account of death of Smita Madhusudan Khedkar, Aged 22 years, who was a student of second year Engineering College, in FA-1910-2012 above traffic accident dated 22.05.2009, by invoking section 166 of M.V. Act, her parents - present appellants instituted M.A.C.P. No.178 of 2009.

Learned Tribunal, after appreciating the case and submission advanced by each of the side, framed issues and held that,
claimants had succeeded in proving that there was rashness and negligence on the part of S.T.
driver, and also in view of the pleading of the respondent, recorded a finding that there was no contributory negligence.

8. While considering the entitlement of compensation, learned Tribunal seems to have taken into account that deceased was college going students, and as pointed out, seems to have considered a notional income of Rs.3,000/- per month i.e. 36,000/- per annum.
However, claimants are seeking enhanced compensation on the ground that inadequate compensation was granted.

However, to maintain unformity, in view of the decision in the case of Navjot Singh (supra) and Khalid Ansari (supra), it would be just and proper to consider income of deceased Smita as 10,000/- per month.

Learned counsel for the appellant has strenuously argued that the award passed by the Tribunal has to be tested on the basis of the decision in Sarla Verma [2009(4) All MR 429 (S.C.)] (supra)
which was holding the field.

It may be mentioned that in Maj. Genl. A.S. Gauraya and Anr v. S. N.
Thakur, AIR 1986 SC 1440 : [1986 All MR ONLINE 227 (S.C.)] the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "there is nothing like any prospective operation alone of the law laid down by the Supreme Court.

entities.text:
Maj. Genl. A.S. Gauraya and Anr v. S. N.
Thakur, AIR 1986 SC 1440 : [1986 All MR ONLINE 227 (S.C.)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The law laid down by the Supreme Court applies to all pending proceedings".
It is also settled proposition that the discretion to restrict the operation of a decision prospectively, vests only with the Supreme Court.

In Pranay Sethi as well as Magma General Insurance, (2018 ALL SCR 2001]
(supra) the Apex Court has no where indicated that the judgment would apply prospectively and not retrospectively.

This being the case, dictum of the Apex Court in Pranay Sethi [2018 ALL SCR 953]
(supra) as well as Magma General Insurance (2018 ALL SCR 2001] (supra) would apply to all pending proceedings.

The appeals being continuation of original proceedings filed before the Tribunal under Section 166 of the M. V. Act, the compensation has to be computed on the basis of the law expounded by the Apex Court in the aforesaid cases."
FA-1910-2012

From the aforesaid observations, it is clearly evident that law laid down by the Apex Court applies not only to the prospective cases, but also to all pending proceedings and even in the pending appeals.
10. The age of deceased reported to be 21 years.

However, In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra) and Pranay Sethi (supra), deceased being bachelor,
half of the income should be deducted for personal expenses and that claimants are also entitled for future prospects to the tune of 40% by applying multiplier of 18 in view of age of deceased.
11. Further, in the considered opinion of this court, learned Tribunal has granted less amount towards loss of consortium, funeral expenses and loss of estate.
In view of the ratio laid down in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra), claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each, i.e. 80,000 /- towards consortium and loss of love and affection.
Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.

ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed with proportionate costs.
(ii) Impugned judgment and award dated 05.01.2012, passed by the learned District Judge -1 and Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Beed in M.A.C.P. No. 178 of 2009, is modified.

(iii) Respondent to pay enhanced compensation of Rs.12,81,500/- to claimants within 12 weeks from today along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of registration of claim petition till its realization.

(vi) On deposit of the amount by respondent, appellants/claimants are permitted to withdraw the same.
